passages.text: These were the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel. Though he was the firstborn, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph son of Israel, because Reuben defiled his father’s bed. So he is not reckoned according to birthright.
passages.sermon:
Reuben was the firstborn son of Israel.
Reuben had the rights of the firstborn.
Reuben defiled his father's bed.
Because of this, Reuben lost his birthright.
The birthright was given to the sons of Joseph, who was also a son of Israel.
Reuben is not counted as the firstborn in the records.
passages.original: וּבְנֵ֨י רְאוּבֵ֥ן בְּכֽוֹר־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ כִּ֣י ה֣וּא הַבְּכוֹר֒ וּֽבְחַלְּלוֹ֙ יְצוּעֵ֣י אָבִ֔יו נִתְּנָה֙ בְּכֹ֣רָת֔וֹ לִבְנֵ֥י יוֹסֵ֖ף בֶּן־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹ֥א לְהִתְיַחֵ֖שׂ לַבְּכֹרָֽה׃

passages.text: And though Judah prevailed over his brothers and a ruler came from him, the birthright belonged to Joseph.
passages.sermon: Judah was stronger than his brothers.\r\nA ruler came from Judah.\r\nThe birthright belonged to Joseph.
passages.original: כִּ֤י יְהוּדָה֙ גָּבַ֣ר בְּאֶחָ֔יו וּלְנָגִ֖יד מִמֶּ֑נּוּ וְהַבְּכֹרָ֖ה לְיוֹסֵֽף׃ס

passages.text: The sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
passages.sermon: Reuben was the firstborn son of Israel.\r\nReuben had four sons.\r\nTheir names were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
passages.original: בְּנֵ֥י רְאוּבֵ֖ן בְּכ֣וֹר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל חֲנ֥וֹךְ וּפַלּ֖וּא חֶצְר֥וֹן וְכַרְמִֽי׃

passages.text: The descendants of Joel: Shemaiah his son, Gog his son, Shimei his son, Micah his son, Reaiah his son, Baal his son, and Beerah his son, whom Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria carried into exile. Beerah was a leader of the Reubenites.
passages.sermon:
Joel had descendants.
Joel’s son was Shemaiah.
Shemaiah’s son was Gog.
Gog’s son was Shimei.
Shimei’s son was Micah.
Micah’s son was Reaiah.
Reaiah’s son was Baal.
Baal’s son was Beerah.
Tiglath-pileser was king of Assyria.
Tiglath-pileser carried Beerah into exile.
Beerah was a leader of the Reubenites.
passages.original: בְּנֵ֖י יוֹאֵ֑ל שְׁמַֽעְיָ֥ה בְנ֛וֹ גּ֥וֹג בְּנ֖וֹ שִׁמְעִ֥י בְנֽוֹ׃ מִיכָ֥ה בְנ֛וֹ רְאָיָ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ בַּ֥עַל בְּנֽוֹ׃ בְּאֵרָ֣ה בְנ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶגְלָ֔ה תִּלְּגַ֥ת פִּלְנְאֶ֖סֶר מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשֻּׁ֑ר ה֥וּא נָשִׂ֖יא לָרֽאוּבֵנִֽי׃

passages.text: His relatives by their clans are recorded in their genealogy: Jeiel the chief, Zechariah, and Bela son of Azaz, the son of Shema, the son of Joel. They settled in Aroer and as far as Nebo and Baal-meon.
passages.sermon:
These men are relatives of the Reubenites.
They belong to different clans.
Their names are recorded in their genealogy.
Jeiel is the chief.
Zechariah is also listed.
Bela is the son of Azaz.
Azaz is the son of Shema.
Shema is the son of Joel.
Bela lived in Aroer.
He also lived as far as Nebo.
He also lived as far as Baal-meon.
passages.original: וְאֶחָיו֙ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֔יו בְּהִתְיַחֵ֖שׂ לְתֹלְדוֹתָ֑ם הָרֹ֥אשׁ יְעִיאֵ֖ל וּזְכַרְיָֽהוּ׃ וּבֶ֙לַע֙ בֶּן־ עָזָ֔ז בֶּן־ שֶׁ֖מַע בֶּן־ יוֹאֵ֑ל ה֚וּא יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בַּעֲרֹעֵ֔ר וְעַד־ נְב֖וֹ וּבַ֥עַל מְעֽוֹן׃

passages.text: They also settled in the east as far as the edge of the desert that extends to the Euphrates River, because their livestock had increased in the land of Gilead.
passages.sermon:
The Reubenites were a tribe of Israel.
They settled in the east.
They lived as far as the edge of the desert.
This desert reached to the Euphrates River.
Their livestock increased greatly.
They had many animals in the land of Gilead.
passages.original: וְלַמִּזְרָ֗ח יָשַׁב֙ עַד־ לְב֣וֹא מִדְבָּ֔רָה לְמִן־ הַנָּהָ֖ר פְּרָ֑ת כִּ֧י מִקְנֵיהֶ֛ם רָב֖וּ בְּאֶ֥רֶץ גִּלְעָֽד׃

passages.text: During the days of Saul they waged war against the Hagrites, who were defeated at their hands, and they occupied the homes of the Hagrites throughout the region east of Gilead.
passages.sermon:
Saul was king during this time.
The Reubenites fought a war against the Hagrites.
The Reubenites defeated the Hagrites.
The Reubenites took the homes of the Hagrites.
The Reubenites lived in these homes.
These homes were in the region east of Gilead.
passages.original: וּבִימֵ֣י שָׁא֗וּל עָשׂ֤וּ מִלְחָמָה֙ עִם־ הַֽהַגְרִאִ֔ים וַֽיִּפְּל֖וּ בְּיָדָ֑ם וַיֵּשְׁבוּ֙ בְּאָ֣הֳלֵיהֶ֔ם עַֽל־ כָּל־ פְּנֵ֖י מִזְרָ֥ח לַגִּלְעָֽד׃פ

passages.text: The descendants of Gad lived next to the Reubenites in the land of Bashan, as far as Salecah: Joel was the chief, Shapham the second, then Jaanai and Shaphat, who lived in Bashan.
passages.sermon:
The descendants of Gad lived next to the Reubenites.
They lived in the land of Bashan.
They lived as far as Salecah.
Joel was the chief among them.
Shapham was the second leader.
Jaanai and Shaphat also lived in Bashan.
passages.original: וּבְנֵי־ גָ֣ד לְנֶגְדָּ֗ם יָֽשְׁב֛וּ בְּאֶ֥רֶץ הַבָּשָׁ֖ן עַד־ סַלְכָֽה׃ יוֹאֵ֣ל הָרֹ֔אשׁ וְשָׁפָ֖ם הַמִּשְׁנֶ֑ה וְיַעְנַ֥י וְשָׁפָ֖ט בַּבָּשָֽׁן׃

passages.text: Their kinsmen by families were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber—seven in all.
passages.sermon: The descendants of Gad had kinsmen by families.\r\nThese kinsmen were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber.\r\nThere were seven kinsmen in total.
passages.original: וַאֲחֵיהֶ֞ם לְבֵ֣ית אֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם מִֽיכָאֵ֡ל וּמְשֻׁלָּ֡ם וְ֠שֶׁבַע וְיוֹרַ֧י וְיַעְכָּ֛ן וְזִ֥יעַ וָעֵ֖בֶר שִׁבְעָֽה׃ס

passages.text: These were the sons of Abihail son of Huri, the son of Jaroah, the son of Gilead, the son of Michael, the son of Jeshishai, the son of Jahdo, the son of Buz.
passages.sermon:
Abihail was a man from the tribe of Gad.
Abihail was the son of Huri.
Huri was the son of Jaroah.
Jaroah was the son of Gilead.
Gilead was the son of Michael.
Michael was the son of Jeshishai.
Jeshishai was the son of Jahdo.
Jahdo was the son of Buz.
These men were ancestors in the family line of Gad.
passages.original: אֵ֣לֶּה׀ בְּנֵ֣י אֲבִיחַ֗יִל בֶּן־ חוּרִ֡י בֶּן־ יָ֠רוֹחַ בֶּן־ גִּלְעָ֧ד בֶּן־ מִיכָאֵ֛ל בֶּן־ יְשִׁישַׁ֥י בֶּן־ יַחְדּ֖וֹ בֶּן־ בּֽוּז׃

passages.text: Ahi son of Abdiel, the son of Guni, was head of their family.
passages.sermon: Ahi was the son of Abdiel.\r\nAbdiel was the son of Guni.\r\nAhi was the head of their family.
passages.original: אֲחִי֙ בֶּן־ עַבְדִּיאֵ֣ל בֶּן־ גּוּנִ֔י רֹ֖אשׁ לְבֵ֥ית אֲבוֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: They lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its towns, and throughout the pasturelands of Sharon.
passages.sermon:
The sons of Abihail lived in Gilead.
They also lived in Bashan.
They lived in the towns of Bashan.
They lived throughout the pasturelands of Sharon.
They lived in all these places with their families.
passages.original: וַיֵּֽשְׁב֛וּ בַּגִּלְעָ֥ד בַּבָּשָׁ֖ן וּבִבְנֹתֶ֑יהָ וּבְכָֽל־ מִגְרְשֵׁ֥י שָׁר֖וֹן עַל־ תּוֹצְאוֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: All of them were reckoned in the genealogies during the reigns of Jotham king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel.
passages.sermon:
Jotham was king of Judah.
Jeroboam was king of Israel.
During their reigns, leaders and families were counted in the genealogies.
All of them were included in these records at that time.
passages.original: כֻּלָּם֙ הִתְיַחְשׂ֔וּ בִּימֵ֖י יוֹתָ֣ם מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֑ה וּבִימֵ֖י יָרָבְעָ֥ם מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

passages.text: The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh had 44,760 warriors—valiant men who carried the shield and sword, drew the bow, and were trained for battle.
passages.sermon:
The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh were tribes of Israel.
They had many warriors.
These warriors were 44,760 in number.
They were valiant men.
They carried shields.
They carried swords.
They drew the bow.
They were trained for battle.
passages.original: בְּנֵֽי־ רְאוּבֵ֨ן וְגָדִ֜י וַחֲצִ֥י שֵֽׁבֶט־ מְנַשֶּׁה֮ מִן־ בְּנֵי־ חַיִל֒ אֲ֠נָשִׁים נֹשְׂאֵ֨י מָגֵ֤ן וְחֶ֙רֶב֙ וְדֹ֣רְכֵי קֶ֔שֶׁת וּלְמוּדֵ֖י מִלְחָמָ֑ה אַרְבָּעִ֨ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֥ה אֶ֛לֶף וּשְׁבַע־ מֵא֥וֹת וְשִׁשִּׁ֖ים יֹצְאֵ֥י צָבָֽא׃

passages.text: They waged war against the Hagrites, as well as Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.
passages.sermon:
The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh were warriors.
They fought a war.
They fought against the Hagrites.
They also fought against Jetur.
They also fought against Naphish.
They also fought against Nodab.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ מִלְחָמָ֖ה עִם־ הַֽהַגְרִיאִ֑ים וִיט֥וּר וְנָפִ֖ישׁ וְנוֹדָֽב׃

passages.text: And because they cried out to God in battle, they were helped against their enemies, and the Hagrites and all their allies were delivered into their hands. Because they put their trust in God, He answered their prayers.
passages.sermon:
The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh fought in battle.
They faced the Hagrites and their allies.
They cried out to God during the battle.
God helped them against their enemies.
God gave the Hagrites and all their allies into their hands.
God answered their prayers because they trusted Him.
passages.original: וַיֵּעָזְר֣וּ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּנָּתְנ֤וּ בְיָדָם֙ הַֽהַגְרִיאִ֔ים וְכֹ֖ל שֶׁ֣עִמָּהֶ֑ם כִּ֠י לֵאלֹהִ֤ים זָעֲקוּ֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְנַעְתּ֥וֹר לָהֶ֖ם כִּי־ בָ֥טְחוּ בֽוֹ׃

passages.text: They seized the livestock of the Hagrites—50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep, and 2,000 donkeys. They also took 100,000 captives, and many others fell slain, because the battle belonged to God. And they occupied the land until the exile.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites fought against the Hagrites and their allies.
The Israelites won the battle.
They captured the Hagrites' livestock.
They took 50,000 camels.
They took 250,000 sheep.
They took 2,000 donkeys.
They also took 100,000 people as captives.
Many enemies died in the battle.
God gave the Israelites victory in the battle.
The Israelites lived in the land they captured.
They stayed there until the exile.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁבּ֣וּ מִקְנֵיהֶ֗ם גְּֽמַלֵּיהֶ֞ם חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אֶ֙לֶף֙ וְצֹ֗אן מָאתַ֤יִם וַחֲמִשִּׁים֙ אֶ֔לֶף וַחֲמוֹרִ֖ים אַלְפָּ֑יִם וְנֶ֥פֶשׁ אָדָ֖ם מֵ֥אָה אָֽלֶף׃ כִּֽי־ חֲלָלִ֤ים רַבִּים֙ נָפָ֔לוּ כִּ֥י מֵהָאֱלֹהִ֖ים הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וַיֵּשְׁב֥וּ תַחְתֵּיהֶ֖ם עַד־ הַגֹּלָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Now the people of the half-tribe of Manasseh were numerous. They settled in the land from Bashan to Baal-hermon (that is, Senir, also known as Mount Hermon).
passages.sermon:
The half-tribe of Manasseh was a group of Israelites.
They had many people.
They lived in the land east of the Jordan River.
They settled from Bashan to Baal-hermon.
Baal-hermon is also called Senir.
Senir is also known as Mount Hermon.
passages.original: וּבְנֵ֗י חֲצִי֙ שֵׁ֣בֶט מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה יָשְׁב֖וּ בָּאָ֑רֶץ מִבָּשָׁ֞ן עַד־ בַּ֧עַל חֶרְמ֛וֹן וּשְׂנִ֥יר וְהַר־ חֶרְמ֖וֹן הֵ֥מָּה רָבֽוּ׃

passages.text: These were the heads of their families: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel. They were mighty men of valor, famous men, and heads of their families.
passages.sermon:
Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel were leaders.
They were the heads of their families.
They were mighty men of valor.
They were famous men.
passages.original: וְאֵ֖לֶּה רָאשֵׁ֣י בֵית־ אֲבוֹתָ֑ם וְעֵ֡פֶר וְיִשְׁעִ֡י וֶאֱלִיאֵ֡ל וְ֠עַזְרִיאֵל וְיִרְמְיָ֨ה וְהוֹדַוְיָ֜ה וְיַחְדִּיאֵ֗ל אֲנָשִׁים֙ גִּבּ֣וֹרֵי חַ֔יִל אַנְשֵׁ֣י שֵׁמ֔וֹת רָאשִׁ֖ים לְבֵ֥ית אֲבוֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: But they were unfaithful to the God of their fathers, and they prostituted themselves with the gods of the peoples of the land, whom God had destroyed before them.
passages.sermon:
The people of the half-tribe of Manasseh were unfaithful to the God of their fathers.
They turned away from Him.
They worshiped the gods of the peoples of the land.
God had destroyed those peoples before them.
They followed the gods that God had already defeated.
passages.original: וַיִּֽמְעֲל֔וּ בֵּאלֹהֵ֖י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּזְנ֗וּ אַחֲרֵי֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י עַמֵּי־ הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־ הִשְׁמִ֥יד אֱלֹהִ֖ים מִפְּנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: So the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria (that is, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria) to take the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh into exile. And he brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river of Gozan, where they remain to this day.
passages.sermon:
The God of Israel acted.
He stirred up the spirit of Pul, king of Assyria.
Pul is also called Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria.
God caused Pul to take the Reubenites into exile.
God caused Pul to take the Gadites into exile.
God caused Pul to take the half-tribe of Manasseh into exile.
Pul brought them to Halah.
Pul brought them to Habor.
Pul brought them to Hara.
Pul brought them to the river of Gozan.
They remain there to this day.
passages.original: וַיָּעַר֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת־ ר֣וּחַ׀ פּ֣וּל מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁ֗וּר וְאֶת־ ר֙וּחַ֙ תִּלְּגַ֤ת פִּלְנֶ֙סֶר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וַיַּגְלֵם֙ לָראוּבֵנִ֣י וְלַגָּדִ֔י וְלַחֲצִ֖י שֵׁ֣בֶט מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה וַ֠יְבִיאֵם לַחְלַ֨ח וְחָב֤וֹר וְהָרָא֙ וּנְהַ֣ר גּוֹזָ֔ן עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃פ
